title: Adic finite-Tor domain of rational constructible lattice representatives
statement:
Fix primes $p\ne\ell$, an integer $a\geq1$, $q=p^a$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$ and its algebraic closure $k$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in the fixed coefficient closure, with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, uniformizer $\varpi_E$ and $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ ($n\geq1$), as in [def-pur-conventions]. Let $T$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Then $T$ is noetherian and finite-dimensional, and $\ell$ is invertible in every local ring of $T$, so the category of [def-weil-pbc-rational-category] is defined on $T$.

Write $\mathcal I_E(T)$ for the integral category [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete] whose raw scalar localization is this rational category. Its objects are exactly the derived-complete integral constructible objects of [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], with the same completed coefficient sheaf and reductions. For each $K_0\in\mathcal I_E(T)$ put
$$K_{0,n}=K_0\otimes^L_{\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,T}}(A_{E,n})_T$$
using [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction]. If the cohomology of $K_{0,1}$ is supported in an interval $[r,s]$ with $r\leq s$, then every $K_{0,n}$ has Tor amplitude in $[r,s]$ [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude]. Such an interval exists for every $K_0$. Hence every integral representative of every rational object lies in $D^b_{ctf}(T,\mathcal O_E)$ of [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], with one Tor interval for all reductions; this includes torsion integral representatives.

proof.text: The field $k$ is Noetherian: its only ideals are $0$ and $k$, so every ascending chain stabilizes. Hence $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is Noetherian, and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] applied to the finite-type structure morphism makes $T$ Noetherian. By [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type], $T$ has finite dimension. Choose integers $u,v$ with $u\ell+vp=1$. Every local ring of the $k$-scheme $T$ has characteristic $p$, so the image of $u$ is an inverse of $\ell$. These verify the geometric hypotheses in [def-weil-pbc-rational-category], and therefore its raw scalar localization is defined on $T$. In Lean, use isNoetherian_of_locallyOfFiniteType, exists_topologicalKrullDim_le and the existing coefficientPrime_isUnit_stalk of [def-pur-conventions].

source.place: Tag 01T6, lemma-finite-type-noetherian; finite-dimensionality as in lem-kun-dimension-finite-type; elementary Bezout calculation for invertibility

proof.text: Apply integralStratifiedPerfectDetailed of [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization]. Step 1 provides Noetherianity and finite dimension. The coefficient prime is a unit in global sections because all its germs are units. This identifies the two integral object predicates through the same projection-normalized completed coefficient comparison. The definition [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed] itself supplies an ordered common cohomology interval for all positive reductions, in particular for index zero.

source.place: Definition 6.5.1; Proposition 6.6.11; Proposition 6.8.11(3), with the completed-coefficient and compatible-witness comparison stated in lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization

proof.text: Map the coefficient-prime unit from each stalk to its residue field and choose the corresponding inverse. Apply the first conclusion of [lem-coef-integral-residue-tor] with the fixed field datum, the coefficient extension, the given integral constructible object and the stipulated residue interval. Its interval hypothesis is precisely set containment in the ordered closed interval. The conclusion is the required Tor amplitude at every positive reduction level. Thus the normalized successive-reduction and Artinian-residue arguments are reused through their existing declaration.

source.place: Statement and proof: the same residue interval controls every positive reduction.

proof.text: For each detailed integral object, take the common ordered interval in [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed] and its index-zero support bound. Step 3 supplies one Tor interval for all positive levels, giving [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. To treat any object of [def-weil-pbc-rational-category], retain its underlying integral object. Restriction along the normalized completed coefficient isomorphism is an equivalence: restriction along its inverse is a quasi-inverse, and both composites identify with identity by the identity on sections and the ring-isomorphism inverse laws. The induced exact functor on derived categories is therefore an equivalence. Choose an inverse image and its counit isomorphism. Isomorphism closure from [lem-weil-pbc-uniform-complete-triangulated] transports the given PBC constructibility to this inverse image; step 2 gives detailed constructibility. Apply the first part to obtain its integral finite-Tor property. This uses neither torsion-freeness nor an alteration of the integral objects.
